- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust downward bias or increase sensitivity to recent lows.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% in 3-5 days), model frequently overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 periods.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive abruptly, model often lags; forecast should adjust 1–2 periods ahead of sentiment turn.
- If model shows steady upward trend with no recent volatility, but true outcome shows mean reversion or sharp drop, reduce forecast slope or introduce early downward bias.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >10% from model in first 5 days, assume momentum bias; adjust forecast to align with sentiment volatility pattern.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “low-high-low” cycles, model tends to overreact to highs; apply smoothing or dampen forecast peaks.
